column1: # sysroots.tsv: the systems imp can make programs for, and where what the link needs of each comes from (tools/imp-sysroot reads it; installed as share/imp/sysroots.tsv).

# Fields, separated by tabs: TRIPLE (what --target= takes), OS and ARCH (the directories of the cruntime repository and of the cache: cruntime/OS/ARCH), the RECIPE that makes the sysroot from the system's own packages (method:argument), and a note.

# A sysroot is the files of that system's C library that a link needs and nothing else: the start files (crt1.o ...), the C library, libgcc, and the matching header files (usr/include) for imp-cimport.

# Methods: debian (the Debian packages of that architecture: libc6, libc6-dev, libgcc-s1, libgcc-N-dev, linux-libc-dev; the last field is the release, debian13 is trixie), alpine (musl, musl-dev, linux-headers and the start files of gcc of Alpine, release alpine322 is v3.22),

# msys2 (the UCRT build of mingw-w64 from MSYS2's repository), zigmac (the Darwin headers and libSystem.tbd of the Zig project's source tarball), mingw (the Debian packages of mingw-w64), cygwin (the Cygwin packages), freebsd, openbsd and netbsd
# (the base set of a release), apple (the SDK of the Mac, which Apple does not let anyone else hand out: from xcrun on a Mac, or a path the user gives).

# A row's OS may have the release in it (linux/debian13, linux/alpine322): the directory of the cache and of cruntime is OS/ARCH; imp-sysroot TARGET@debian12 or TARGET@alpine321 makes another release of the same distribution.

column5: macOS: Zig's copy of the Darwin headers and libSystem.tbd (or the SDK of a Mac, with xcrun or --apple-sdk)
